title: First-principles calculations of internal conversion processes in spin defects
authors: Stefano Paolo Villani, Yu Jin, Giulia Galli
abstract: Optically active spin defects are foundational for quantum technologies, yet common approximations underestimate their internal conversion (IC) rates by orders of magnitude. We propose a broad, predictive framework to compute IC rates that incorporates multi-configurational effects via many-body wavefunctions in TDDFT, and includes all-phonon-mode contributions via analytical non-adiabatic couplings. Our approach resolves discrepancies with experiment, achieving quantitative agreement for the NV$^-$ center in diamond, and identifying a previously overlooked non-radiative channel in the divacancy triplet lifetime in SiC.
summary: The paper presents a rigorous theoretical framework to calculate non-radiative internal conversion rates in key spin defects like $	ext{NV}^-$ and $	ext{V}V^0$. By incorporating multi-phonon effects using advanced TDDFT techniques, the authors achieve quantitative agreement with experimental measurements. This work is vital for advancing solid-state quantum technologies by accurately modeling decoherence pathways.
main_problem: Common approximations severely underestimate the internal conversion (IC) rates in optically active spin defects, necessitating a full theoretical treatment of non-radiative decay pathways.
main_result: The proposed framework achieves quantitative agreement with experiment for $	ext{NV}^-$ in diamond and resolves discrepancies regarding the triplet lifetime in $	ext{SiC}$ by incorporating all phonon modes.
method: The study uses a predictive theoretical framework combining Time-Dependent DFT (TDDFT) with hybrid functionals to calculate non-radiative transition rates ($\Gamma_{NR}$) via multi-phonon coupling, including analytical derivatives of non-adiabatic couplings.
model_or_system: The research focuses on optically active spin defects, specifically the $	ext{NV}^-$ center in diamond and the divacancy ($	ext{V}V^0$) center in silicon carbide ($	ext{SiC}$), which are foundational platforms for quantum technologies.
key_observables: Non-radiative transition rates ($\Gamma_{NR}$), excited state lifetimes ($	au$), electron-phonon spectral density function $D(E)$, and adiabatic energy differences ($\Delta_{IF}$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T=4 	ext{ K}$ to $400 	ext{ K}$), specific transitions like $1	ext{A}_1 ightarrow 1	ext{E}$, and the comparison between different DFT functionals (PBE vs. DDH).
main_assumptions: The calculations employ the displaced harmonic oscillator approximation, and initial comparisons highlight that single-mode or accepting-mode approximations are inadequate.
figures_summary: Figures compare calculated non-radiative rates ($\Gamma_{NR}$) using different methods (e.g., all modes vs. localized mode) against experimental lifetimes; other figures show spectral densities $D(E)$ and functional dependencies of these rates.
paper_structure: The paper develops a comprehensive theoretical framework for IC processes, applies it to $	ext{NV}^-$ in diamond and $	ext{V}V^0$ in $	ext{SiC}$, compares results across different computational approximations (e.g., PBE vs. DDH), and validates the methodology against established experimental measurements.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the fundamental physical mechanisms governing spin relaxation in solid-state quantum emitters, which is crucial for designing reliable quantum memory and processing elements.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic representation of the electronic energy levels of the NV−center in diamond and of the VV0 center in silicon carbide. Both systems exhibit a triplet ground state (3A2) and triplet excited state (3E), and two singlet shelving states, 1A1 and 1E, all labeled according to the C3v point group. In an optical cycle, after a laser excitation from 3A2 to 3E, the system can either return to the ground state or transition to 1A1 through inter-system crossing (ISC); from 1A1 the electron then relaxes to 1E, through non-radiative spin-conserving transitions (internal conversion, IC), and fi- nally to the ground state through a second ISC process.
